title: Quiet batch warmup probes scratchpad
content:
Quick thinking doc for a low-noise warmup plan to reduce spike risk during regional flips. Not a final runbook — more of a personal lab notebook.

Context:
- Motivation: recent tiny spikes when switching traffic to eu-west. Hypothesis: cold KV caches + sudden batching patterns cause transient CPU/GPU stalls and 3–6s tail latency blips. Need a smoother handoff that doesn't rely on large synthetic floods (we annoy customers).
- Goal: a small, slow, measurable warmup that exercises hot paths (KV lookups, attention cache priming, short/long seqs) without creating production alarm noise.

Design constraints / requirements:
- No >1% visible increase in 95p latency for production customers in target region during warmup window.
- Telemetry must be granular: per-route, per-model, by seq-length bucket, token-rate buckets.
- Warmup should be reversible mid-run and idempotent — safe to abort.
- Keep traffic footprints tiny (1–5 qps per cohort), but vary payload shapes.

Warmup components (sketch):
1) Quiet cohort sequence
   - Create cohort id: warmup-quiet-<region>-<date> (e.g. warmup-quiet-eu-20251110)
   - Start at 0.1 qps for 10 minutes, 0.5 qps next 10m, 1 qps next 10m (example). Total ramp 30m.
   - Use SDK token scoping to pin to target deployment and model version (allow fallback disabled).

2) Payload mix (rotate every minute):
   - 60% short prompts (<=40 tokens) to hit fast-path and KV lookup dominance
   - 30% medium (100–300 tokens) to exercise KV streaming behavior and batching kernel selection
   - 10% long (600–1024 tokens) to surface memory/kv-edge issues and attention kernel tails

3) Probe types and goals
   - Priming probes: deterministic short prompts that touch common prefixes (e.g., "Summarize: <small doc>") to seed prefix caches.
   - Noise probes: filler random tokens to exercise sampling path — ensure we exercise top-k kernels.
   - Regression probes: golden prompt set from evals (3 prompts) to check semantic output drift — record embeddings + similarity after each step.

4) Batching knobs (what we tune during warmup):
   - Max batch size soft cap: lower slightly for first 15m to avoid burst coalescing -> prevents large spikes. (e.g., runtime.conf.batch.max_soft=64 -> 48)
   - Aggressive batching window: keep conservative early (hold 5ms) then relax.
   - KV cache retention tune: ensure priming CPI touches TTL to avoid early eviction; set warmup-specific TTL policy if supported.

5) Observability checklist (pre-warmup baseline capture):
   - Per-model 50/95/99 latency, per-token p95, error rate, OOM events last 24h
   - GPU util distribution across pods (mean + tail)
   - Scheduler queue time and batch size distribution
   - Memory pressure / mmap churn alerts

Telemetry queries (notes to self — adapt to bq/metrics):
- Latency by seq bucket: SELECT approx_percentile(latency_ms, 0.95) FROM metrics WHERE seq_len_bucket IN ("short","medium","long") AND model = 'gptx-3' GROUP BY seq_len_bucket
- Token throughput: SUM(tokens) / SUM(interval_seconds) by deployment
- Batch size histogram: use existing metric batch.size_bucket{deployment} for 1h window

Abort criteria (immediate stop if any triggered):
- p95 for production routes increases > 1.2x baseline for more than 2 continuous minutes
- error-rate delta > 0.5 percentage points absolute
- OOM or GPU-throttle event occurs in target pool

Safe rollback plan:
- Pause warmup generator -> wait 30s to clear in-flight requests -> remove cohort routing -> re-route any diverted traffic back to stable model version.
- If warmup causes deterioration, disable warmup batching overrides and revert to steady config (git PR rollback link in linked_artifacts).

Execution steps (quick runbook draft):
1) Create warmup cohort config in Console (route: warmup-quiet-eu, tag: internal-warmup)
2) Register client tokens scoped to deployment, schedule generator job in infra-staging cluster (k8s cronjob w/ quiet-prober image)
3) Start with 10m baseline collection (no warmup) -> record metrics snapshot
4) Start ramp as per component #1, watch Telemetry dashboard and Slack #rollouts-live
5) At each step (10m marks) capture snapshot, run 3 regression prompts, compute embedding similarity to baseline; if delta > threshold (0.07) pause and investigate

Commands / snippets (for reuse):
- curl warmup prober (example)\n  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $WARMUP_TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"gptx-3","input":"Summarize: The quick brown...","routing":{"cohort":"warmup-quiet-eu"}}'

- bq query (pseudo)\n  bq query --use_legacy_sql=false '\n    SELECT seq_bucket, APPROX_QUANTILES(latency_ms,100)[OFFSET(95)] as p95 FROM `redwood.prod.metrics` WHERE deployment="eu-west" AND timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() GROUP BY seq_bucket'\n
Open questions / unknowns (investigate before next run):
- Can Console create ephemeral TTL-lift for KV caches per cohort? If not, consider adding a lightweight mutation to runtime to honor warmup tag. (TODO: file runtime RFC)
- Does warmup traffic influence autoscaler signals (pod CPU/RPS)? We need to ensure warmup cohorts are excluded from certain autoscale metrics or accounted-for in scaling policy. Action: ask SRE (Jamal).
- Embedding similarity thresholds — choose conservative defaults. Talk to Eval team to standardize.

Notes on customer noise minimization:
- Use internal-only cohort labels so alerts that filter by customer-visible routes ignore warmup.
- Keep rate very low; use multiple distinct tiny tokens rather than bursts that mimic legitimate heavy customers.

Post-warmup validation (10–60m):
- Run golden set 10x and compare logits/statistics to baseline; check perplexity shifts, embedding cosine means.
- Confirm no tail latency drift and no error ramp.
- Record a short postmortem with timestamps of cohort ramp and metric snapshots.

If this goes well: next steps / experiments
- Try micro-cohort parallel warmups to prime specific tenant buckets before a tenant flip.
- Evaluate warmup TTL policies (runtime change) vs client-side synthetic priming (client SDK seeds).
- Automate warmup -> canary transition when steady metrics persist for N intervals.

Personal TODOs before next run:
- [ ] Sync with Jamal on autoscaler metric exclusions (INF-4234 assigned)
- [ ] Draft lightweight runtime change RFC for cohort TTL handling
- [ ] Create a small internal prober image with payload rotation and registry stamp
- [ ] Build a dashboard template (per-deployment warmup view) and put on Console templates

Random lab notes (brain-dump):
- Observed once that medium-length requests cause increase in batch.window due to kernel switch; need to capture timeline correlation between scheduler queue depth and kernel selection logs.
- Might be useful to tag probes with a header indicating payload shape so post-hoc queries can slice without relying on seq-length inference.

End of scratchpad — will refine after Jamal sync.
